nodes.label: desktop memory - the v3 question id scheme

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. Decided and built 2026-06-22. HERB questions carry no native id - answerable ones are dicts of {question, ground_truth, citations, type} and unanswerable ones are bare strings, both addressed only by array position - so v3 mints a stable id from each question's physical coordinate: <product-stem>::<a|u>::<index>, for example ActionGenie::a::0 and ActionGenie::u::3. The a|u marker is required rather than decoration, because both arrays are 0-indexed so without it answerable[0] and unanswerable[0] collide. The scheme is deterministic by sorted product files and enumerate, collision-free and verified unique across all 1,514 questions - 815 answerable plus 699 unanswerable - and traces back to the exact raw record, making it the paired-test join key. The answerable index equals HERB's answerable_questions position, so cross-build comparison pairs on (product, index) and NOT on the id string, whose format is build-local. It lives in v3/questions.py as mint_id() plus load_questions(raw_root, ids=None), reading raw only under truth quarantine so pipelines never import it, with the ids filter EXACT so an unmatched id raises and there is no silent cohort shrink. The record shape is {id, question, type, ground_truth, citations} with no answerable field, cut as redundant
